architecture_principles: a discovered material regularity is only usable inside the chemistry family in which it was measured
a scientific applicability boundary is executable code, not prompt advice
the language model may criticize the rule and may not override it
value of information is computed by a deterministic tool over the admissible set only
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
every gate decision carries a machine-readable reason and is serialized with the run

arm_difference_declaration.forbidden_confound: Hiding applicability information from V5_NO_GATE while showing it to V5_FULL is prohibited by protocol v1.1.
held_identical: model endpoint and stage model assignment
evidence access profile and filtered evidence state
raw assess_shared_shape_applicability outputs for every candidate
the full inadmissible-card list and its machine-readable reasons
VOI implementation, weights and tie epsilon
arm_difference_declaration.information_parity_evidence: build_pre_enforcement_payload() takes no arm argument, and its SHA-256 is written into every run as pre_enforcement_payload_sha256. The two arms must report the same hash.
arm_difference_declaration.only_intended_difference: whether the identical chemistry-domain applicability audit is enforced as hard experiment-card admissibility before VOI and at freeze
arm_difference_declaration.payload_consequence: Both arms receive the same audit, the same per-candidate applicability outputs and the same inadmissible-card list. V5_NO_GATE marks the audit advisory and keeps every card selectable; V5_FULL marks it binding and removes the inadmissible cards from the ranked set.

candidate_space.rationale: V5 reuses the byte-identical V3/V4 lattice so that the measured change is the chemistry-domain constraint, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> mandatory chemistry-audited local science tool -> deterministic chemistry-domain applicability audit (identical and model-visible in both arms) -> enforcement (V5_FULL only) -> VOI over the selectable set -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze

rules: M-HOLD-120 is admissible: it measures thermal-hold drift directly and does not use the shared thermal-response shape.
M-REPEAT is admissible: it measures realization/state spread directly.
M-SWEEP is admissible: it is the direct verification measurement for a chemistry-shifted candidate.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use equal to allowed_with_state_anchor, or when configs/verified_shape_transfer.json records a completed direct sweep for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification. This is deterministic inadmissibility, not a VOI penalty and not prompt advice.

architecture.claim_boundary: V5.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime with a deterministic chemistry-domain admissibility constraint. A V5 result is evidence about executable scientific constraints on measurement choice. It is not a wet-lab result and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.manuscript_boundary: V5 run results must not be written into manuscript/MAIN_TEXT_V5.md or manuscript/SUPPLEMENTARY_INFORMATION_V5.md until the run series is audited and explicitly frozen by the author.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_CHEMISTRY_GATED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V5
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information or admissibility
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
re-running, rewriting or reinterpreting the frozen V4 series

primary_arms.role: advice-only control isolating the incremental effect of turning identical scientific applicability information into an executable hard constraint
prospective chemistry-aware Agent V5 with executable scientific constraints

architecture.purpose: Test whether an experimentally discovered material regularity and its chemistry-domain boundary can be executed as a hard scientific constraint on which measurement an outcome-blind Agent is allowed to select.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question the next experiment must answer, and request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations
execute read-only scientific tools. The chemistry-audited local rheology summary is mandatory and is forced into the trace whether or not the planner requested it.

deterministic, non-LLM measurement-applicability audit. Computed once per run without reference to the arm, fully visible to the model in both arms, serialized in full, and never produced by a model stage.
V5_FULL only. Converts the identical audit into hard admissibility before VOI ranking and again at freeze. It cannot be overridden by any model stage.
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value from the cards present in the payload
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability and whether its falsification criterion can actually be met
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported weight sensitivity and the strongest objection
commit to one experiment card present in the payload, or abstain, and state its acceptance and falsification criteria
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card. A selection outside the admissible set is rejected at freeze rather than repaired.

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V5 is a new prospective runtime. configs/agent_v4.json, scripts/run_agent_v4.py, prompts/agent_v4_*.txt, src/pur_new/voi.py and every frozen V3/V4 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V5.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards

decision_stability_sent_to_model.evaluated_over: the selectable experiment cards of this arm
decision_stability_sent_to_model.metric_is_not: model confidence; posterior probability; calibrated expected information
decision_stability_sent_to_model.voi_formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: Using matched reference measurements and uncertainty below 3.4%, accept exactly one level hypothesis if the measured S1C41 viscosity-level change is within plus or minus 3.4 percentage points of its registered prediction: -42.76% for H-LEVEL-DILUTE, 17.24% for H-LEVEL-ASSOC, or -72.76% for H-LEVEL-PLASTIC. Report the directly measured 120 and 130 C viscosity levels with the accepted formulation-level classification.
judge_normalized.chemistry_support_statement: The processing-window viscosity level is measured directly in the selected resin_modified:ac1920+tk100 chemistry, so it does not depend on transferring a rheological regularity from the unmodified chemistry family. E_eta is a rheological fit obtained directly for S1C41 and supports only a formulation-level temperature-response statement for S1C41; it does not establish transfer to other resin-modified chemistries or a molecular mechanism.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: H-LEVEL-DILUTE is falsified if the measured level change is outside [-46.16%, -39.36%]. H-LEVEL-ASSOC is falsified if the measured level change is at or below -42.76% or is not within [13.84%, 20.64%]. H-LEVEL-PLASTIC is falsified if the measured level change is at or above -42.76% or is not within [-76.16%, -69.36%]. If the result lies within none of the three acceptance intervals, all three registered level explanations are rejected at the 3.4% resolution. These outcomes falsify only the corresponding formulation-level prediction, not a molecular mechanism.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: Run S1C41::M-HOLD-120 with at least two independent repeats, measuring viscosity at 120 C at 15, 30, 45, and 60 minutes and reporting SI_15_to_60; use this to test the unresolved candidate-specific hot-hold failure. If axis attribution is required afterward, run a single-axis candidate experiment from the supplied card set.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: Directly measured viscosity level change at 120 and 130 C relative to a matched unmodified reactive-core reference, together with the fitted apparent temperature-response descriptor E_eta from ln(eta) versus 1/T over 80-130 C.
judge_normalized.rationale: S1C41::M-SWEEP is the most scientifically defensible card because S1C41 is resin-modified chemistry without verified shared-shape transfer. It directly measures the 120-130 C processing-window level, separates the three registered level predictions at the stated resolution, and provides a local rheological temperature-response descriptor. The result must be interpreted as a composition-level rheological test; the separate 120 C drift failure remains unresolved.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: I followed the Proposer and Robustness Adjudicator over the deterministic ranking. The deterministic top cards were unsupported M-ANCHOR experiments tied at the highest score, but the advisory chemistry audit identifies their reconstructed processing-window observable as outside validated chemistry support. M-SWEEP directly measures the decision quantity in S1C41 and tests, rather than assumes, the temperature response. I also adopt the Skeptic's requirements for a matched unmodified reference, uncertainty below 3.4%, and no claim that M-SWEEP tests hot-hold stability.

uncertainty_decomposition.evidence_coverage_uncertainty: The three level hypotheses are registered phenomenological predictions, but the experiment changes AC1920 and TK100 together and cannot identify either modifier's separate contribution.
uncertainty_decomposition.extrapolation_uncertainty: The viscosity level and fitted E_eta are local to S1C41. No shared-shape transfer to the broader resin-modified family is established.
uncertainty_decomposition.measurement_uncertainty: Direct-sweep discrimination is approximately 3.4%; matched reference measurements and repeats or uncertainty estimates must establish uncertainty below 3.4 percentage points.
uncertainty_decomposition.realization_state_uncertainty: Preparation-to-preparation state variation is not removed by M-SWEEP; matched batch, operator, process history and repeat measurements are required.

planner.chemistry_support_statement: The local rheological regularities were measured in the original PUR reactive-core family, including the acrylic-like and minor tackifier-like modifier axes, with a separate E1 plus-phosphoric-acid perturbation check. The intended experiment stays inside this family only if it uses those registered modifier families without introducing a chemistry-changing modifier such as AC1920 or TK100; otherwise shared-shape transfer is unsupported and a direct temperature sweep is required.
planner.failure_mode: Excessive isothermal viscosity drift during the 120 C residence period, with candidate-specific drift risk unresolved.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The original E5 formulation shows SI_15_to_60 = 0.515 and SI_15_to_90 = 0.931 at 120 C, versus 0.095 and 0.168 for E1, demonstrating large local variation and a potentially unacceptable thermal-hold failure.
planner.least_resolved_justification: Only two original formulations have thermal-hold observations, both at 120 C with four time points from 15 to 90 minutes; no follow-up mean profiles are available and candidate-specific hold behavior is unmeasured. In contrast, temperature response has seven original sweep runs across 80-130 C, while viscosity-level behavior for a new candidate remains unmeasured but is directly testable by a sweep.
measurement_requirements: Directly measure the candidate and matched unmodified reactive-core reference across 80-130 C in 10 C increments on freshly prepared samples, rather than reconstructing the processing-window level from a single anchor.

Report the realized viscosity level at 120 and 130 C and the apparent temperature-response descriptor from ln(eta) versus 1/T, with sufficient repeat information to distinguish differences larger than the approximately 3.4% direct-sweep discrimination threshold.
Use the measured level relative to the declared inert-dilution prediction to distinguish at least the dilution, acrylic-association, and plasticization hypotheses.
Measure the candidate at 120 C at 15, 30, 45, and 60 minutes in at least two independent repeats and report SI_15_to_60 to test whether the local thermal-drift failure is reproduced.
planner.scientific_question: For a candidate containing the registered modifier axes, does its realized viscosity level at matched temperature follow inert dilution, rise above dilution as predicted by acrylic association, or fall below dilution as predicted by plasticization, and does the candidate maintain an acceptable isothermal trajectory at 120 C?

proposer.chemistry_support_assessment: The candidate uses AC1920 and TK100 at 15% and 5%, respectively, within the externally supported intervention regions, but this modified chemistry is outside the family in which the shared thermal-response shape was measured. M-SWEEP is therefore appropriate because it measures the processing-window viscosity directly and does not rely on transferring the unvalidated shared shape. The result can verify or reject shape transfer while directly testing the level hypotheses.

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: If the directly measured 120-130 C level change falls within the 3.4% direct-sweep resolution of exactly one registered prediction for S1C41—approximately -42.76% for H-LEVEL-DILUTE, 17.24% for H-LEVEL-ASSOC, or -72.76% for H-LEVEL-PLASTIC—that hypothesis is supported for this composition and the directly measured processing-window level is reported.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: H-LEVEL-DILUTE is falsified if the measured change differs from -42.76% by more than 3.4%. H-LEVEL-ASSOC is falsified if the measured change is at or below -42.76%, and H-LEVEL-PLASTIC is falsified if it is at or above -42.76%. A result satisfying none of the acceptance bands would reject all three registered level explanations at this resolution.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A result between prediction bands or within the direct-sweep resolution of more than one prediction is non-discriminating at this measurement precision; it would not establish a unique level hypothesis, although the directly measured temperature response would still test whether the unmodified-family shape transfers to this chemistry.

proposer.primary_observable: Directly measured viscosity level at 120 and 130 C across the 80-130 C sweep, with the apparent temperature-response descriptor E_eta from ln(eta) versus 1/T.

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: It has the highest deterministic VOI but reconstructs the 120-130 C observable from a shared shape that has not been verified for the AC1920/TK100 chemistry, making its primary observable chemistry-inadmissible before direct shape verification.
It directly addresses the established 120 C drift failure but does not measure the processing-window level and cannot separate the three registered level hypotheses.
It characterizes preparation-to-preparation state spread but does not directly return the candidate processing-window level or discriminate the registered level hypotheses.

proposer.reasoning: The deterministic top set consists of M-ANCHOR cards tied at 0.739167, but the audit is advisory and independently identifies those anchors as unsupported before shape verification. S1C41::M-SWEEP directly measures the decision quantity in the modified chemistry, preserves full discrimination among all three registered level hypotheses, and simultaneously verifies the temperature-response shape rather than assuming it. The candidate also lies within the supported 15-25% acrylic-like and 3-10% minor-tackifier-like intervention regions.

robustness_adjudication.change_from_proposal: No change to the proposed experiment card. Retain S1C41::M-SWEEP, but require a matched unmodified reactive-core reference under the same protocol, repeats or uncertainty estimates sufficient to establish resolution below 3.4%, and separate M-HOLD-120 measurements if hot-hold stability is part of the decision. Interpret E_eta as a fitted rheological descriptor and do not generalize shape transfer beyond S1C41.
robustness_adjudication.departure_from_deterministic_ranking: The Proposer departed from the deterministic tied top set of unsupported M-ANCHOR cards and selected S1C41::M-SWEEP. This departure is scientifically justified because S1C41 is resin-modified chemistry outside the measured shared-shape support, whereas M-SWEEP directly measures the processing-window level and tests shape transfer.
residual_decision_risk: S1C41-specific 120 C hold drift remains unresolved by M-SWEEP and requires M-HOLD-120.
Changing AC1920 and TK100 together does not identify the separate contribution of either modifier axis.
A direct sweep verifies thermal response only for S1C41 and does not validate transfer to the broader resin-modified chemistry family.
The fitted E_eta descriptor remains model-dependent and is not a molecular activation or association mechanism.
Preparation-state variability and reference uncertainty may still limit discrimination if the added repeat and matching protocol are inadequate.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The strongest objection identifies that the proposed level comparison is not operationally defined at the claimed 3.4% resolution without a matched unmodified reactive-core reference and repeat or uncertainty information. It does not change which experiment should be run: M-SWEEP remains the appropriate card, but it must be interpreted only as a composition-level comparison after adding the matched reference and sufficient repeats. The objection also means that M-SWEEP alone does not test the candidate-specific 120 C hold trajectory; that requires the separate M-HOLD-120 protocol.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: The deterministic tied top set is unchanged across all reported weight perturbations: top_experiment_set_stability is 1.0, intervention_family_stability and measurement_plan_stability are 1.0, and recommendation_flip_boundary reports no flips for any weight term over the 0.5x-1.5x sweep. The base margin to the first strictly lower experiment is 0.002292. These results describe stability of the transparent score, not confidence or correctness. The Proposer's M-SWEEP departure remains scientifically defensible under all reported weightings because the tied M-ANCHOR cards rely on an observable outside their measured chemistry support; weight rescaling cannot repair that limitation.

skeptic.chemistry_domain_support_assessment: The primary S1C41 viscosity level stays inside the measured support only in the limited sense that M-SWEEP measures it directly in the resin_modified:ac1920+tk100 chemistry. The proposal correctly avoids transferring the unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI shared shape through M-ANCHOR. The fitted E_eta descriptor remains a rheological fit, not a molecular mechanism, and any shape-transfer claim is local to S1C41 unless additional resin-modified sweeps verify broader transfer.
skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: A direct sweep can produce a measured 120-130 C level and compare it with the three predictions, whose minimum separation is about 30 percentage points and therefore exceeds the stated 3.4% direct-sweep resolution. In practice, the protocol must add an explicitly matched unmodified reactive-core reference and sufficient repeats or uncertainty estimates; otherwise the criterion is formally measurable but not reliably attainable at its declared resolution.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The result could support or reject one of the three static-level hypotheses, but it cannot support the broader claim that S1C41 maintains an acceptable isothermal trajectory at 120 C.
objections.objection: For S1C41, the three registered level predictions are separated by more than the declared M-SWEEP resolution: -72.76%, -42.76% and 17.24% versus 3.4%, so the direct sweep can discriminate the registered formulation-level hypotheses. However, the experiment does not cover the separate stability hypotheses or the candidate-specific 120 C hold trajectory described in planner.scientific_question and planner.measurement_requirements.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Any axis-specific or molecular attribution would be unsupported; only a composition-level classification among the three aggregate level predictions would be justified.
objections.objection: S1C41 changes both modifier axes simultaneously: AC1920 is 15% and TK100 is 5%, with reactive_mass_fraction 0.8. Consequently, a measured departure from the -42.76% dilution prediction cannot be attributed separately to the acrylic-like axis or the minor-tackifier-like axis. The registered hypotheses are separable as aggregate predictions at this composition, but the experiment cannot identify whether an elevation is caused by acrylic association or whether a depression is caused by one or both modifier axes acting as plasticizers.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The level comparison may be improperly normalized, and any mechanistic interpretation based on E_eta would exceed what the measurement establishes.
objections.objection: The viscosity level at 120 and 130 C is directly measured by M-SWEEP, but the accompanying E_eta descriptor is obtained by regressing ln(eta) against 1/T. Thus E_eta is fit-dependent, and it should not be treated as a directly observed chemical activation quantity. In addition, the acceptance criterion requires a level change 'against the unmodified reactive core', while the proposer.protocol specifies only a fresh S1C41 sweep and does not explicitly include a matched unmodified-reference sweep or a contemporaneous reference measurement.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A successful S1C41 sweep could be overgeneralized into a validated shared-shape rule for the broader resin-modified chemistry family.
objections.objection: The proposer correctly identifies S1C41 as chemistry_family resin_modified:ac1920+tk100 with applicability_status modified_chemistry_unvalidated and selects M-SWEEP rather than M-ANCHOR. The direct 80-130 C sweep therefore does not reuse the unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI shared shape as the primary level measurement. The remaining limitation is that the sweep verifies the thermal response only for S1C41; it does not establish transferability to other resin-modified compositions.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A result near a prediction boundary could be labeled as support or falsification without demonstrating that preparation and reference uncertainty are below the declared 3.4% resolution.
objections.objection: The direct-sweep criterion is experimentally reachable because M-SWEEP measures 120-130 C viscosity directly and the prediction separations exceed 3.4%. However, measurement_catalog.M-SWEEP specifies min_repeats 1, while the proposer gives no repeat or uncertainty protocol for distinguishing a candidate/reference level difference at the 3.4% resolution. The criterion also depends on a matched unmodified-core comparison that is absent from proposer.measurement_plan.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The experiment could be reported as resolving both static level behavior and hot-hold stability, or as proving molecular association/plasticization, although neither claim follows from the specified protocol.
objections.objection: M-SWEEP cannot answer the candidate-specific hot-hold question. Its protocol ends with the 80-130 C sweep and ln(eta) versus 1/T regression; it contains no 120 C measurements at 15, 30, 45 and 60 minutes. The proposer therefore cannot claim that the experiment tests the established drift failure, even though the planner identifies drift as the least-resolved coordinate. Also, rheology alone cannot establish a molecular association or plasticization mechanism; it can only compare the realized level with the registered phenomenological predictions.

skeptic.recommended_change: Retain M-SWEEP but explicitly run a matched unmodified reactive-core reference under the same batch, operator and temperature protocol, add repeats sufficient to establish uncertainty below 3.4%, and append the M-HOLD-120 protocol at 120 C with measurements at 15, 30, 45 and 60 minutes. Interpret the level result only as a composition-level discrimination; use a separate single-axis experiment if attribution of AC1920 versus TK100 is required.
skeptic.strongest_objection: The acceptance criterion compares the measured S1C41 level change with predictions relative to the unmodified reactive core, but proposer.measurement_plan specifies only one fresh 80-130 C sweep of S1C41 and does not explicitly measure the matched unmodified reference. Without that reference and repeat information, the central -42.76%, 17.24% and -72.76% comparisons are not operationally defined with the claimed 3.4% resolution.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The verified E1 +P phosphoric-acid perturbation is excluded from the primary same-composition fit and is interpreted separately as a chemical-perturbation check.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.
Keep deliberately chemistry-perturbed curves outside same-composition fitting, but use them to test whether an intervention shifts viscosity scale, thermal-response shape, or both.

chemical_perturbation_check.interpretation: The verified low-dose H3PO4 perturbation shifts the observed viscosity level while remaining closely compatible with the local shared thermal-response geometry. It is a separate chemical-perturbation check and is not pooled into the primary same-composition state model.

observational_E1_GJJ_day1_comparator.interpretation_boundary: Observational reference only; the compact record does not establish a paired parent-batch relationship between E1 +P and E1 GJJ day-1.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.
experiment_design_implications.verified_acid_perturbation: E1 +P received 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution during dehydration. Its close agreement with the primary shared thermal shape makes it useful as a defined scale-versus-shape perturbation check, not as another nominal E1 realization.

provenance_audit.reason: E1 +P is a verified chemical perturbation: 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution was added during dehydration. It is excluded from the same-composition primary state model and exposed separately as a perturbation check.

tool_trace.name: get_candidate_hypothesis
tool_trace.reason: Retrieve the evidence-derived candidate-space hypothesis and modifier-axis boundaries needed to formulate a prospective experiment without using follow-up identity or outcomes.

evidence: PAT_US20160215185A1: repeated acrylic tackifying resin examples at approximately 19-20% of total formulation
PAT_US6465104B1 Example 10: 25 wt% low-OH acrylic copolymer with direct 121 C viscosity-stability data
PAPER_CN_ADHESIVES_2025_34_09_54: reports a 15% preferred acrylic-resin addition level, retained as directional lower-bound evidence until its fraction denominator is reverified
acrylic_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 20 and 25% are directly commensurate coarse anchors in the current curated record. The 15% grid level is retained as a lower-bound design point, but the literature denominator for the reported 15% addition level is not treated as an exact total-formulation anchor until reverified.

evidence: PAT_US5932680A: examples around 4.8-6.4% tackifying/hydrocarbon resin and preferred resin range 3-10 wt%
PAT_US20070155859A1: tackifiers/rheology-control agents typically used below about 10 wt%
minor_tackifier_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 5% represents the repeatedly documented minor-resin region and 10% is a conservative coarse upper level.

result.claim_boundary: External examples are analogues. They support candidate-family and coarse-region hypotheses, not an exact optimum for AC1920/TK100 and not a proven local molecular mechanism. The current reconstruction uses only pre-result evidence at runtime; the exact validation coordinates and outcome are excluded from candidate construction, ranking and tie-breaking.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

local_reactive_core_anchor.reason: E2 is the geometric centre of the original five-point local design: 50/50 PPG2000/PDP-70 and NCO:OH=1.80, centered between E1/E3 stoichiometric perturbations and E4/E5 composition perturbations.
local_reactive_core_anchor.stoichiometry_note: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 label applies to the original reactive core. If a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.

chemistry_applicability_audit.enforcement_note: In this condition the chemistry applicability audit is ADVISORY. Every experiment card above remains selectable, including the cards the audit marks inadmissible. Use the audit as scientific evidence and justify whatever you select.
rule_text: Scope: measurement admissibility, not formulation admissibility.
M-HOLD-120, M-REPEAT and M-SWEEP observe their quantity directly and remain admissible.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use == 'allowed_with_state_anchor', or when a versioned prior direct sweep has verified transferability for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification: the one-point anchor would reconstruct 120-130 C viscosity through a shape that has never been measured for that chemistry.
This audit is a deterministic scientific rule, not a VOI penalty and not a model opinion. Whether it is binding in this run is stated by the enforcement field.

voi.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.
voi.tie_note: These experiments share an identical component vector. The deterministic tool is indifferent among them. Any choice within this set must be justified scientifically.

top_cards.required_precondition: a completed direct M-SWEEP on this chemistry family, recorded in configs/verified_shape_transfer.json

top_cards.acceptance_criterion: The measured 120-130 C level change against the unmodified reactive core falls within 8.80% of exactly one registered prediction: -59.00% for H-LEVEL-DILUTE, 31.00% for H-LEVEL-ASSOC or -95.00% for H-LEVEL-PLASTIC. That hypothesis is accepted for this composition and the processing-window level is reported with it.
top_cards.admissibility_reason: M-ANCHOR reconstructs the 120-130 C response through the shared thermal-response shape. That shape has not been measured for chemistry family resin_modified:ac1920+tk100 (applicability status modified_chemistry_unvalidated), and no versioned prior direct sweep has verified its transfer.

budget_efficiency_detail.definition: 1 - effort_points / max(effort_points) over the declared catalog

top_cards.falsification_criterion: H-LEVEL-ASSOC is falsified if the measured level change is at or below the inert-dilution prediction of -59.00%. H-LEVEL-PLASTIC is falsified if it is at or above that same prediction. H-LEVEL-DILUTE is falsified if the measured level change departs from -59.00% by more than the 8.80% resolution of this plan.
